_comment: EXPECTED TO DIFFER PER SITE. The budgets tests/page-weight.spec.ts checks (decoded kilobytes).
Set 2026-10-27 from what each page weighed (Playwright, chromium) plus about 25%. Route keys match tests/routes.ts (no trailing slash).
Keys left out fall back to the spec's own numbers. A route that must be heavy gets its own entry under pages, with the reason in _why.
jsonLd lists the schema.org types a route must carry, e.g. { "/": ["Organization"] }.

maxScriptKb lowered from 430 to 120 by overhaul 1.4 (2026-10-30): the React chrome islands became small .astro scripts, so every route except /photography ships no React. Measured after (with 1.2 merged): about 16 KB of script files per route (the chrome scripts are small enough that Astro inlines them), against about 342 KB before. The margin leaves room for the overhaul's own scripts (1.7's motion switch and the like) without hiding a framework creeping back. The /contact override (2650 KB) went the same day: its 2101 KB was React plus the form libraries, and /contact now weighs what every other page does. The Google Maps iframe there is created by a script only when its box nears the viewport (since overhaul 1.5; loading=lazy alone fetched it with the page once the column got shorter), so its 1.7 MB of third-party script is only fetched (and counted) once a visitor scrolls to it.

/._why: The hero reel shows real client sites as images (about 13 small WebP captures, 2026-10-30). The WebGL hero and its 1237 KB of three.js were removed the same day, so scripts fall back to the default budget.

/work/stone-steps-50k._why: The sample case study (Stone Steps, since 2026-10-30). Lowered by overhaul 2.4b (2026-10-31): the site showcase became 'Walk the homepage', which crops the 1440x10824 capture to its first 4,000px at build time (ruling 4) and drops the floating phone. Measured in Playwright chromium after: 403 KB of images (was 875), the largest one the 145 KB walk capture (the full-length capture was one 504 KB WebP). The budget is that plus about 25%, so it sits just above the 500 KB default; the per-image cap is the walk capture plus margin.
